mainTopic: When does a שומר who lies about a פקדון pay תשלומי כפל (double payment)? The גמרא finishes a teaching about a found אבידה, then quotes a משנה from later in the מסכת and draws two lessons from it: only a טענת גנב, and only with a שבועה, brings כפל.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a teaching: someone guarding a lost object he found pays כפל, from the פסוק ״על כל אבדה״. Then the גמרא quotes a משנה about a שומר who swears falsely about a פקדון. If he claimed ״it got lost,″ he pays only the קרן. If he claimed ״it was stolen,″ he pays כפל. From this the גמרא learns that only a טענת גנב, and only one made with a שבועה, brings כפל. Two ברייתות argue over whether ״אם ימצא הגנב״ is about the real thief or the lying שומר. Both agree that ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ is about the lying שומר, and רבא explains how the words show this. A גזירה שוה on ״שליחות יד″ shows that the שומר must have sworn. The גמרא then works out how each ברייתא gets its sources: excluding a claim of loss, the four-or-five payment of רבי חייא בר אבא, and a real thief's own כפל. The answer to that last question, a teaching of תנא דבי חזקיה, begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: A found lost object also brings double payment
steps.stepSummary: The end of the previous teaching: someone holding a lost object he found pays תשלומי כפל if he lies about it, based on the פסוק ״על כל אבדה אשר יאמר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a lost object, he pays double payment, as the פסוק says: ″For any lost thing about which one shall say.″
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of a teaching that started before this section. It says the double-payment rule also covers a lost object someone found and is holding for its owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about כפל mentions ״אבדה″ (a lost item), so the teaching learns that a finder who is guarding a lost item is treated like a שומר. If he falsely claims a thief took it, he pays double just like a regular שומר would.

keyTerms.meaning: A lost object that someone found and must hold until he returns it
Double payment, the penalty a thief pays
As it says (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this ״אבידה″ up with the ״טענת אבד″ coming later. Here אבידה means a found object being guarded. Later, ״אבד″ means a שומר's claim that a פקדון got lost.

phrases.english: With a lost object, he pays double payment;
phrases.notes: He means a lost item someone found and is now holding for the owner.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "For any lost thing about which one shall say."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder who lies about a found lost object he is guarding pays כפל, learned from ״על כל אבדה״.

steps.title: The משנה's first case: the guard claims the deposit was lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a שומר swears falsely that the פקדון got lost, and witnesses show he ate it. He pays only the קרן. If he confesses on his own, he pays קרן, חומש and brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: ″Where is my deposit?″ He said to him, ″It got lost.″ ″I make you swear,″ and he said ″Amen.″ Then witnesses testify that he ate it. He pays the principal. If he admitted it himself, he pays the principal, a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from another place. This is the first of two cases in that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שומר lied and swore, but his lie was ״it got lost,″ not ״it was stolen.″ So when witnesses catch him, he only pays back the value of the item, with no double. If he confesses before witnesses come, he gets the special rules for a false oath about money: an extra fifth and a קרבן אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
A deposit, something given to a שומר to guard
I make you swear (an oath imposed by the owner)
The principal, the actual value of the item
An extra fifth added to the payment
A guilt-offering brought to atone for a false oath

phrases.english: We learned there: "Where is my deposit?"
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later, on בבא קמא 108b. The owner is asking the guard.

phrases.english: He said to him: "It got lost."
"I make you swear," and he said: "Amen";
phrases.notes: Answering ״אמן″ to the owner's oath counts as swearing it himself.

phrases.english: and the witnesses testify about him that he ate it –
he pays the principal.
If he admitted it by his own word –
he pays the principal and a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line of discussion by quoting a משנה from another place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Falsely swearing ״it got lost″: if caught by witnesses, he pays קרן only. If he confesses, he pays קרן, חומש and brings an אשם.

steps.title: The משנה's second case: the guard claims the deposit was stolen
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה continues: a שומר swears falsely that the פקדון was stolen, and witnesses show he stole it himself. He pays כפל. If he confesses on his own, he pays קרן, חומש and brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: ″Where is my deposit?″ He said to him, ″It was stolen.″ ″I make you swear,″ and he said ″Amen.″ Then witnesses testify that he stole it. He pays double payment. If he admitted it himself, he pays the principal, a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case that is almost the same as the first. The only difference is that the guard claimed ״stolen″ instead of ״lost.″
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because his false claim blamed a thief, the תורה treats him like a thief himself, and he pays double when witnesses catch him. The confession case stays exactly the same as before: קרן, חומש and an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stolen
He admitted on his own, before witnesses came
Witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: Putting the two cases side by side shows that the kind of false claim (״lost″ or ״stolen″) is exactly what decides whether he pays כפל.

phrases.english: "Where is my deposit?" He said to him: "It was stolen."
"I make you swear," and he said: "Amen";
and the witnesses testify about him that he stole it –
he pays double payment.
If he admitted it on his own –
he pays the principal and a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה with the contrasting case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Falsely swearing ״it was stolen″: if caught by witnesses, he pays כפל. If he confesses, he pays קרן, חומש and brings an אשם.

steps.title: Two lessons from the משנה: only a theft claim, and only with an oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws two points from the משנה. First, only a טענת גנב brings כפל, not a טענת אבד. Second, even a טענת גנב brings כפל only if he said it with a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the משנה teaches that one who claims ″a thief took it″ pays double, but one who claims ″it got lost″ does not pay double. And even one who claims ″a thief took it″ pays double only with an oath. Without an oath, he does not pay double.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and pulls out two lessons from it. These lessons set up the next move in the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lesson one comes from comparing the two cases: ״lost″ brought only קרן, while ״stolen″ brought כפל. Lesson two comes from noticing that the משנה's case of כפל includes a שבועה. This suggests that a lie without an oath would not bring כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (pointing out what we can learn from a source)
The claim that a thief stole the deposit
The claim that the deposit got lost
With an oath

steps.whatToRemember: According to this משנה, כפל for a שומר needs two things: a טענת גנב (not a טענת אבד), and a שבועה backing up the lie.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches that one who claims "a thief took it"
pays double payment –
but one who claims "it got lost"
does not pay double payment.
And even one who claims "a thief took it" –
it is with an oath that he pays double payment,
but without an oath
he does not pay double payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה just quoted and draws lessons from comparing its two cases.
steps.raayaObject: Two conditions for a שומר's כפל: the claim must be a טענת גנב, and it must be made with a שבועה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on בבא קמא 108b: ״lost″ brings only קרן, ״stolen″ brings כפל, and the כפל case includes a שבועה.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the rule of כפל for a טענת גנב comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the פסוק behind the rule just learned from the משנה. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed from the משנה that a false טענת גנב brings כפל. Now the גמרא wants the source for this in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: "These matters" means the rule from the last step: a false claim that a thief stole the item brings כפל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule drawn from the משנה in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches כפל for a false טענת גנב.

steps.title: First ברייתא: the פסוק is about the false claimer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says ״אם ימצא הגנב״ speaks about a שומר who falsely claims a thief stole the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "If the thief shall be found" — the פסוק is speaking about someone who makes the claim that a thief stole it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It reads the פסוק ״אם ימצא הגנב״ as talking about a lying שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "the thief" in this פסוק are read as the שומר who pretends a thief came. He is the one who pays כפל. That gives us the source for כפל on a false טענת גנב.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who claims that a thief stole the item
The פסוק is speaking about

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"If the thief shall be found"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:6

phrases.english: the verse is speaking of one who claims a thief stole it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״אם ימצא הגנב״ refers to a שומר who falsely claims a thief took the item.

steps.title: First ברייתא proves its reading from the next פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פסוק might mean the real thief. It proves its reading from ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it is about one who claims a thief stole it — or maybe it is only about the thief himself? When it says "If the thief shall not be found," the פסוק is speaking about one who claims a thief stole it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא considers another way to read the פסוק, as speaking about the real thief. It then rejects that by pointing to the next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק, ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״, clearly speaks about the lying שומר, because no other thief was found. Since the two פסוקים sit together, the first one is read as speaking about the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opens a check of the reading)
The real thief himself
When the פסוק says (brings a proof)

phrases.english: You say it refers to one who claims a thief stole it —
or is it only about the thief himself?
When it says: "If the thief shall not be found"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:7

phrases.english: the verse is speaking of one who claims a thief stole it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּגַנָּב עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the reading given in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That ״אם ימצא הגנב״ refers to the טוען טענת גנב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The next פסוק, ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״, which speaks about the lying שומר.

steps.title: Second ברייתא: the פסוק is about the real thief
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says ״אם ימצא הגנב״ speaks about the actual thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: "If the thief shall be found" — the פסוק is speaking about the thief himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that reads the same פסוק the opposite way. It says the פסוק is about the real thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the first פסוק teaches that a real thief who is caught pays כפל. This argues with the first ברייתא's reading of that פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא teaches

phrases.english: Another baraita teaches:
"If the thief shall be found"
the verse is speaking of the thief himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reading that argues with the one in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״אם ימצא הגנב״ speaks about the actual thief.

steps.title: Second ברייתא: the next פסוק already covers the false claimer
steps.stepSummary: Since ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ already covers the lying שומר, the first פסוק must be about the real thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it is about the thief himself — or maybe it is only about one who claims a thief stole it? When it says "If the thief shall not be found," the false claimer is already mentioned. So how do I explain "If the thief shall be found"? The פסוק is speaking about the thief himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The second ברייתא proves its reading. The next פסוק already teaches about the lying שומר, so the first פסוק must teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות use the same next פסוק, but in opposite ways. The first ברייתא says the two פסוקים speak about the same case. The second says the תורה would not repeat itself, so the first פסוק must be about a different case: the real thief.

keyTerms.meaning: It is already stated
How do I explain (what does this פסוק still teach)?

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות quote the very same פסוק as their proof. The first says it shows the two פסוקים are about the same case. The second says it shows the first פסוק must be about something else.

phrases.english: You say it refers to the thief himself,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב?
phrases.english: or is it only about one who claims a thief stole it?
When it says: "If the thief shall not be found"
the one who claims a thief stole it is already stated,

phrases.aramaic: הָא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים: ״אִם יִמָּצֵא הַגַּנָּב״?
phrases.english: so how do I explain "If the thief shall be found"?
phrases.notes: He means: if both פסוקים were about the lying שומר, the first one would teach nothing new.

phrases.english: The verse is speaking of the thief himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the reading given in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That ״אם ימצא הגנב״ refers to the actual thief.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The next פסוק already covers the טוען טענת גנב, so the first פסוק must teach a different case.

steps.title: Both agree about the second פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ is about a שומר who falsely claims a thief stole the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, according to everyone, "If the thief shall not be found" is written about one who claims a thief stole it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what the two ברייתות agree on. Both read the second פסוק as speaking about the lying שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: However they read the first פסוק, both ברייתות agree on the second one. So the source for כפל on a false טענת גנב holds for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone
In any case, at least

steps.whatToRemember: ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ is the agreed source that a שומר who falsely claims a thief stole the item pays כפל.

phrases.english: In any event, according to everyone,
"If the thief shall not be found"
is written about one who claims a thief stole it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the two ברייתות in steps 6 to 9 agree on.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All agree that ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ teaches כפל for a false טענת גנב.

steps.title: How do the words show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ is understood to mean the lying שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What shows this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the words of the פסוק point to the lying שומר. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, "if the thief is not found" sounds like a real thief who was not caught. The גמרא wants to know how we get to a שומר who lied.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows this? How is it implied?

phrases.english: From where is this inferred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the reading agreed on in step 10 fits the words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the words ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ point to a lying שומר.

steps.title: רבא: it was not found as he said
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the פסוק as: if it is not found to be as the שומר said, but he stole it himself, he pays double.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: "If it is not found" to be as he said, but rather he himself stole it — he pays double.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the words. "Not found" means the שומר's story turned out to be false, because he took the item himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads "not found" as being about the שומר's claim, not about a missing thief. The claim proved false, so the שומר is the thief and he pays כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: As he said (his claim)
He pays double (כפל)

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading ties the כפל to the שומר's false claim. That is exactly the case of the משנה in step 3.

phrases.english: Rava said:
"If it is not found" to be as he said,
but rather he himself stole it —
he shall pay double.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אִם לֹא יִמָּצֵא כְּמָה שֶׁאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״אם לא ימצא״ means the שומר's claim was not found to be true, since he stole it himself, so he pays כפל.

steps.title: How do we know the lying שומר must have sworn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the כפל of a טוען טענת גנב applies only when he took a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that this applies only when he took an oath?
steps.whatsHappening: Having just shown that ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ is about the lying שומר, the גמרא now asks how we know he pays כפל only if he swore falsely. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying to the owner is not enough. The rule is that the שומר pays כפל only after he swears to his false claim. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
An oath
Double payment

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is with an oath?
phrases.notes: He means that the lying שומר pays double only if he swore to his false story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״ is about the lying שומר, and asks about one more condition of his כפל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the lying שומר's כפל requires a שבועה.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads 'approaching the judges' as coming to swear
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that ״ונקרב בעל הבית אל האלהים״ means the שומר comes to court to take a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And the homeowner shall approach the judges' means for an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It reads the words 'shall approach the judges' in the פסוק about the lying שומר as meaning he comes to court to swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same פסוק that begins ״אם לא ימצא הגנב״. If his going to the judges means taking a שבועה, then his כפל is tied to that oath. The next lines prove this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall approach
Here it means the judges

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'And the homeowner shall approach
phrases.notes: שמות 22:7. The 'homeowner' here is the שומר, the person the item was left with.

phrases.english: the judges' — for an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְנִקְרַב בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶל הָאֱלֹהִים״ – לִשְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק's 'approach the judges' means approaching to take a שבועה.

steps.title: Maybe he only comes to court for judgment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks itself whether 'approach the judges' might just mean coming to be judged, not to swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means for an oath, or perhaps only for judgment?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. Maybe going to the judges just means standing trial. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'approach the judges' do not say 'oath' outright. Another reading is possible: he simply comes to court. The ברייתא needs proof that a שבועה is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (a test of whether a reading is the right one)
Judgment, a court case

phrases.english: Do you say it means for an oath,
or is it only for judgment?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לִשְׁבוּעָה, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading just given in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'approach the judges' means a שבועה or only a court case.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from 'laying a hand' proves it means an oath
steps.stepSummary: The words 'שליחות יד' appear in both פסוקים. Since the later פסוק is clearly about a שבועה, the earlier one is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Laying a hand' is said below, and 'laying a hand' is said above. Just as there it is for an oath, so too here it is for an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its reading with a גזירה שוה. The same phrase appears in two פסוקים, so the two are linked, and they share the same meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later פסוק openly mentions 'the oath of ה׳' together with 'שליחות יד'. The earlier פסוק uses 'שליחות יד' too, so it also speaks of an oath. That shows the lying שומר's כפל comes only after he swears.

keyTerms.meaning: Laying a hand: using the deposit for oneself
Below, in the later פסוק
Above, in the earlier פסוק
Just as there, so too here (the language of a גזירה שוה)

steps.whatToRemember: The טוען טענת גנב pays כפל only if he swore falsely. We learn this from a גזירה שוה on 'שליחות יד'.

phrases.english: 'Laying a hand' is stated below,
phrases.notes: שמות 22:10, which speaks openly about 'the oath of ה׳'.

phrases.english: and 'laying a hand' is stated above;
phrases.notes: שמות 22:7, our פסוק about approaching the judges.

steps.title: Why are two פסוקים needed if both speak of the lying שומר?
steps.stepSummary: With one פסוק for the real thief and one for the lying שומר, two פסוקים make sense. But if both are about the lying שומר, why repeat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for the one who says one פסוק is about the thief and one is about the one claiming a thief took it, that is why two פסוקים are written. But for the one who says both are about the one claiming a thief took it, why do I need two פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the two ברייתות from earlier. It challenges the opinion that both פסוקים about כפל speak of the lying שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opinion that one פסוק is about a real thief has no problem, because each פסוק teaches something different. But if both פסוקים teach the same case, one of them seems extra. The גמרא wants to know what the extra one adds.

steps.title: One פסוק excludes a false claim that the item was lost
steps.stepSummary: The second פסוק teaches that a שומר who falsely claims the item was lost does not pay כפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: one פסוק comes to exclude a claim that it was lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra פסוק has a job. It limits כפל to a false claim of theft and leaves out a false claim that the item was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים are about the lying שומר. One teaches that he pays כפל. The other narrows the rule to a claim that a thief took the item, so someone who falsely swears it was lost does not pay double.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude

steps.whatToRemember: Only a false claim of theft (טענת גנב) leads to כפל. A false claim of loss (טענת אבד) does not.
steps.confusionAlert: A שומר who lies and swears that the item was lost still pays back the item itself. He just does not pay the extra double.

phrases.english: They say: one comes to exclude a claim that it was lost.

steps.title: Where does the second ברייתא (one פסוק for the thief) learn that a false claim of loss is excluded?
steps.stepSummary: According to the opinion that one פסוק is about a real thief and one is about the lying שומר, no פסוק is extra. So where does he learn that a false claim of loss pays no כפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the one who says one פסוק is about the thief and one is about the שומר who claims a thief took it, so no פסוק is extra, where does he learn to exclude a claim that the item was lost?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion. It asks where that opinion gets the rule from Step 18, that a שומר who falsely claims loss does not pay כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18, the opinion that both פסוקים are about the שומר used the repeated פסוק to exclude a false claim of loss. The second ברייתא uses each פסוק for a different case, so it has no extra פסוק for that lesson. The גמרא wants to know his source.

steps.title: He learns it from the extra ה in ״הַגַּנָּב״
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said ״גַּנָּב״ but says ״הַגַּנָּב״. That extra ה limits the rule to a claim of theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: From 'a thief' versus 'the thief'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first opinion learns the exclusion from one extra letter in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added ה, meaning 'the,' points to a specific case: a claim that a thief took the item. That narrows כפל to a claim of theft and leaves out a claim of loss. This opinion needs no extra פסוק, only the extra letter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A thief' versus 'the thief.' The extra ה teaches something

phrases.english: From 'a thief' versus 'the thief.'

steps.title: What does the first ברייתא (both about the שומר) learn from ״הַגַּנָּב״?
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that both פסוקים are about the lying שומר already excluded a claim of loss using the extra פסוק. So what does he do with the extra ה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says both are about one who claims a thief took it, who already excluded a claim of loss, what does he learn from 'a thief' versus 'the thief'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the opposite question. If the second opinion already has a source for excluding loss, what is the extra ה teaching him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra word or letter should teach something. The second opinion used the repeated פסוק for the exclusion of loss, so ״הַגַּנָּב״ seems to have no job. The גמרא asks what he learns from it.

steps.title: It is needed for the rule of רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: The extra ה teaches רבי חייא בר אבא's rule in the name of רבי יוחנן. A שומר who falsely claims theft pays כפל, and if he slaughtered or sold the animal he pays four or five times.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you that it is needed for what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן. One who falsely claims a thief took a deposit pays double. If he slaughtered or sold it, he pays four or five times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second opinion uses ״הַגַּנָּב״ for a different rule: treating the lying שומר exactly like a real thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the regular rules, a real thief who slaughters or sells an ox or sheep pays four or five times. The extra ה teaches that the lying שומר counts as 'the thief' in every way, so he gets this payment too, not only כפל.

steps.title: The four-or-five payment comes from a juxtaposition
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא learns that the lying שומר pays four or five times from a הקש between the thief and the שומר, and a הקש cannot be refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can tell you: it is a הקש, and we do not argue against a הקש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 23. The first opinion learns the four-or-five payment of the lying שומר from a הקש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה places the real thief and the lying שומר side by side. Because of that, whatever the thief pays, the שומר pays too, including four or five times. Someone might point out differences between the two cases, but a הקש works even when the cases are not fully alike.

keyTerms.meaning: A הקש: a comparison of two cases that the תורה places side by side, so the same law applies to both
We do not refute a הקש by pointing out differences between the two cases
He can tell you (introduces how this opinion would answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a הקש can be knocked down like a logical argument. A קל וחומר can be refuted by showing a difference, but a הקש is a direct comparison from the פסוק, so differences do not break it.

phrases.english: He can tell you: it is a juxtaposition,
phrases.notes: The thief and the lying שומר sit side by side in the פסוקים, so the four-or-five payment carries over to the שומר.

phrases.english: and one cannot refute a juxtaposition.

steps.title: Where does the second opinion learn a real thief's double payment
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא has a פסוק for the real thief. If both פסוקים are about the lying שומר, where does the first ברייתא learn that an actual thief pays כפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says one פסוק is about the thief and one is about the lying שומר. But for the one who says both are about the lying שומר, where does he learn the law of the thief himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question against the second opinion. If both פסוקים are about the lying שומר, nothing is left to teach that a real thief pays כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion uses one פסוק for the real thief, so he has a clear source. The second opinion used up both פסוקים on the lying שומר. The real thief's כפל now seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (introduces the side that has no problem, before raising a difficulty)

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the lying שומר does not work
steps.stepSummary: One might learn the thief's כפל by a קל וחומר from the lying שומר. But דיו limits the result to the source, so the thief would pay only if he swore, like the שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let it come by a קל וחומר from the one who claims a thief stole it. It is enough for what is learned from a דין to be like its source: just as there it is with an oath, so too here it would be with an oath!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer, a קל וחומר, and right away rejects it. The rejection uses the rule of דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic goes: if a שומר who only claims theft pays כפל, a real thief should surely pay. But דיו says a law learned this way cannot be stronger than its source. The שומר pays only after a false שבועה, so the thief would also pay only after an oath. That is not the הלכה, so this source fails.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible answer that is about to be rejected)
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case

keyTerms.meaning: What is learned from a קל וחומר is only as strong as its source
An oath

steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר itself is logical. The problem is only that דיו would bring the oath condition along with it, while a real thief pays כפל even without swearing.

steps.title: The thief's double payment comes from תנא דבי חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא learns the real thief's כפל from the teaching of תנא דבי חזקיה, which begins: had the פסוק said only ״שור״ and ״גניבה״, everything would be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from what the school of חזקיה taught. The school of חזקיה taught: let it say ״שור״ and ״גניבה״, and everything would be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 25. The second opinion learns the real thief's כפל from a teaching of the school of חזקיה, which the גמרא now begins to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching is about a separate פסוק about a thief caught with the stolen animal (שמות 22:3). It says that writing just ״שור״ and ״גניבה״ would already have covered all items. That raises the question of why the extra animals are listed, and the answer will serve as the source. This gives a real thief a source that needs no oath.

A teaching from the study house of חזקיה
Theft (the stolen item)

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a source for the thief's כפל that does not depend on the lying שומר, so no oath is required.

steps.title: The narrow reading: only things brought on the altar
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי חזקיה explains what we would have thought if the פסוק were written that way. Since the named detail (an ox) is something brought on the מזבח, only things brought on the מזבח would be included. The only thing that adds is a sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had been written this way, I would have said: just as the detail it names is clearly something brought on the altar, so too only things brought on the altar are included. What would that let you add? A sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the teaching of תנא דבי חזקיה by showing a mistaken 'I would have thought' reading. It is setting up the next move, which will show why this reading is too narrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תורה names a specific item, we include only things similar to it. Here the similarity is 'brought on the מזבח', since an ox is a קרבן animal. Under that rule, the only new thing added would be a sheep, so כפל would be very limited. The teaching will next explain how the actual wording of the פסוק avoids this result.

keyTerms.meaning: The specific detail or item named in the פסוק
Clearly stated or defined
Something that can be brought as a קרבן on the altar
I would have said. This introduces a mistaken first assumption
A sheep or goat

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the final הלכה. It is only what we would have thought if the פסוק were worded differently. The גמרא brings it up in order to reject it.

phrases.english: Had it been written this way, I would have said:
phrases.notes: "This way" means the wording just mentioned in step 27, where the פסוק says only ״שור״ and ״גניבה״.

phrases.english: Just as the detail is clearly defined
phrases.notes: The detail is the specific animal the פסוק names, the ox.

A sheep,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teaching of תנא דבי חזקיה introduced in step 27 by laying out the narrow 'I would have thought' reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Part of the answer from step 27: the derivation starts by showing that a simpler wording would limit כפל to things brought on the מזבח, which adds only a sheep. This sets up why the actual wording is needed.
